segments.text: Good morning everyone, today we continue with linear operators.
Will this be on the exam?
Yes. Let's recall the definition of an eigenvalue first.
Of course. A scalar lambda is an eigenvalue of A if there is a nonzero vector v with A v equal to lambda v.
So the null space of A minus lambda I is nontrivial.
Exactly. Now let's compute the characteristic polynomial.
Is the determinant always a polynomial in lambda?
Good question — yes, of degree n. Let's see why on the board.
